advisor.subtitle: Reads your live book & the market — ranked by what to deal with first.

items.title: Directional risk — net Δ 126.9
items.detail: You're long the market: a 1% drop costs roughly $7,822. Delta is the cheapest greek to remove — flatten it first, then look at your vol risk.

plan.why: Use the index FUTURE, not options: it's delta-1 with no gamma, vega or theta and the tightest spread, so it kills pure directional risk without adding new greeks. Sell ≈ 127 future units to bring net Δ ≈ 0.

items.title: Vol exposure — vega -1694/pt
items.detail: Vega -1694 → you lose about $1,694 per vol point. You're short vol — fine while calm, painful on a spike.

plan.why: Vega is densest at-the-money, and a ~60-day ATM option is liquid and vega-rich (~$9.9/vol-pt per lot). Buy ≈ 171 ATM 6175 calls to offset your short vega. Note it also brings some long gamma and about 91 delta — clean that up with the future afterward.

items.title: Short gamma — exposed to a jump
items.detail: You're short gamma. It's quiet now (realised 6.7% vs implied 17.3%), but a sudden move forces you to hedge into it at a loss. Keep size modest or buy a little gamma back.

plan.why: Gamma concentrates in SHORT-dated at-the-money options, so a ~21-day ATM option flattens gamma with the least vega baggage. Buy ≈ 29 ATM 6175 calls. It brings about $171/vol-pt of vega and ~15 delta — re-hedge that delta with the future.

items.title: Hedging is eating your edge
items.detail: You've paid $307 in hedge costs against $358 of captured edge. Every option hedge crosses the spread — prefer the cheaper future for delta and don't over-trim small greeks.

items.title: Time decay -42/day
items.detail: You pay $42/day in theta — the rent for being long gamma/vega. Worth it only if the market moves enough to scalp it back.

items.title: Cheapest hedge: axe your quotes to the flow you want
items.detail: Paying up in the market costs the spread every time. The cheapest hedge is the next client trade that offsets you — you cut risk AND get PAID the edge (a negative-cost hedge) instead of paying it. Wait for a client SELLING you vol (a straddle / strangle / option you buy), and lean your prices UP to win client SELLS. Each live RFQ in your queue is tagged ↓ (helps) or ↑ (hurts) so you can lean into the right flow.

head: ⚖︎ Hedge the book together
greeks interact — don't chase them one at a time
joint.why: Hedges interact — one option moves delta, gamma AND vega at once, so flattening greeks one at a time chases your tail. Solve them together: a SHORT-dated ATM (gamma-rich) and a LONG-dated ATM (vega-rich) zero your gamma and vega at the same time, then the FUTURE mops up the leftover delta and adds nothing else, so it goes last. Suggested: sell 4 × 21d ATM 6175, buy 101 × 180d ATM 6175, then sell 182 × future.
